premise: A Harbor Commission safety inspector investigates the reported voluntary departure of a remote lighthouse keeper, reconstructing the night from log books, weather records, supply manifests, and radio logs.
setting: Remote coastal lighthouse station on an exposed rock station with supply landing, keeper quarters, lamp gallery, maintenance workshop, and records office
investigator_character: Harbor Commission safety inspector dispatched to verify keeper status and reconstruct the overnight timeline
opening_situation: You arrive by rotor to find relief keeper Sarah Chen waiting on the landing. Assistant keeper Tom Reed claims head keeper Henry Walsh departed voluntarily at 0430, but the station records disagree.
initial_observable_facts: The landing shows storm debris and an unloaded personal trunk tagged for Henry Walsh.
The lamp is operating, but keeper handover was not completed.
Tom Reed has already logged a voluntary departure in the keeper's log.
Commission radio expects your reconstruction report by 1300.
in_world_duration: one inspection day (approximately four in-world hours)
location_scale: single remote lighthouse station with five primary locations
content_boundaries: no graphic violence; no supernatural elements; workplace negligence and cover-up themes; death by accidental fall; no sexual content
required_themes: one perfect ending and several imperfect endings
deadline_or_constraint: Commission report due at 1300; landing weather may close again
author_notes: Codename: The Harbor Light Signal. Culprit NPC-TOM covered up keeper death during unauthorized lens repair. Emphasis on logs, weather, manifests, and radio traffic — not theft.
